boj-officials-signal-rate-hikes-every-fe.headline: BOJ officials signal rate hikes every few months; 30yr JGB yields at 3.88%, 10yr at 2.61% — carry trade unwind risk acute
boj-officials-signal-rate-hikes-every-fe.summary: The 10-year JGB yield dropped to 2.755% on October 23 (below MUFG's Q4 forecast floor of 2.85%) as Takaichi's explicit rejection of Abenomics-style reflation calmed near-term BoJ-behind-the-curve fears, yet the 30-year JGB yield remains near 3.93% (auction Oct 8: 4.109%), reflecting a persistent long-end fiscal risk premium as the FY2027 budget — the Takaichi administration's first full cycle — remains unfunded.
boj-officials-signal-rate-hikes-every-fe.rationale: Both named JGB indicators in s2_japan are updated: the 30-year yield remains elevated at ~3.93% (auction cleared at 4.109%), confirming the long-end fiscal premium persists. The 10-year's drop below 2.8% — while calming near-term carry-trade risk — reflects flight-to-haven demand from global risk aversion (AI selloff, Middle East) rather than fiscal improvement, keeping the 'Takaichi plan financing clarity' sub-indicator at 1 (unclear): the FY2027 budget has no deficit-bond solution yet. Net assessment: short-end calm, long-end stress intact.

synchronized-global-sovereign-bond-rout-.headline: Synchronized global sovereign bond rout: US 10y at 4.80%, UK 30y at 5.82% (highest since 1998), German 10y at 2011 highs
synchronized-global-sovereign-bond-rout-.summary: The 10-year OAT/Bund spread hit 174.6 bps on Oct 22 (171.8 bps on Oct 23), with French 10-year yields at 5.05%, after the National Assembly finance committee rejected the 2027 budget revenue package 31-to-3, injecting acute political risk ahead of the April 2027 presidential election. Early contagion signals are visible in Italian and Spanish spreads, and Moody's already holds France at Aa3 with a negative outlook.
synchronized-global-sovereign-bond-rout-.rationale: The OAT-Bund spread at 171.8 bps — now wider than Italy and Greece — is a direct, named indicator in s10_france. The budget's parliamentary collapse (finance committee 31-3 rejection) also escalates the 'Govt stability' sub-indicator from 1 (fragile) toward 2 (collapse-or-snap-election risk), and Moody's negative outlook keeps the 'Rating action' sub-indicator at 1 with downgrade risk rising. This is the most acute near-term eurozone financial-stability signal of the week.

coreweave-bond-yields-hit-16-stock-40-in.headline: CoreWeave bond yields hit ~16%, stock -40% in October: GPU-backed debt refinancing stress turns acute across neocloud sector
coreweave-bond-yields-hit-16-stock-40-in.summary: CoreWeave's ~$50–52 billion debt load triggered a simultaneous stock and bond selloff — bonds implying 15–16% yields, CDS spreads above 11%, stock down ~40% in October — spreading to Oracle and dragging the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down >13% in October. Elon Musk warned debt markets have 'almost entirely shut off access' for AI data-center companies without independent revenue, signaling sector-wide refinancing stress rather than a single-name event.
coreweave-bond-yields-hit-16-stock-40-in.target_indicator: GPU-backed debt refinancing stress (0 none / 1 signs / 2 acute)
coreweave-bond-yields-hit-16-stock-40-in.rationale: CoreWeave's bond yields at 15–16% and CDS spreads >11%, combined with Musk's statement that debt markets have shut off for neocloud firms, directly activates the 'GPU-backed debt refinancing stress' indicator from 1 (signs) to 2 (acute). The AI capex-vs-revenue gap indicator also widens (CoreWeave guiding $35–39B capex vs ~$13B revenue). The Philadelphia Semis -13% in October further registers in AI-circular-financing systemic risk. This is the clearest single new data point for s8 this week.

houthi-attacks-push-brent-to-117-6-month.headline: Houthi attacks push Brent to $117 (6-month high); Iran accelerates Hormuz surveillance with new naval units; October flows volatile and below pre-war average
houthi-attacks-push-brent-to-117-6-month.summary: Brent crude briefly topped $117/bbl on Oct 23 after Yemen's Houthis launched fresh attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities and the port of Yanbu, while Iran deployed new military units to expand surveillance of the Strait of Hormuz. Although some daily crude readings near prewar levels, October-to-date Middle East exports remain below pre-war averages, ~40% of oil is bypassing Hormuz via alternatives, and Saudi Aramco's CEO warned inventory rebuilding could take up to two years.
houthi-attacks-push-brent-to-117-6-month.rationale: Fresh Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and Iranian Hormuz surveillance escalation directly update s20_sea_lanes. WTI/Brent at ~$113–117 is a live indicator reading. The Hormuz/Red Sea status indicator should remain at 1 (contested) given that flows are partial and volatile with convoy rerouting. This also has cascading effects on s5_china_deflation (cost-push via energy), s18_food_fertilizer (fertilizer input disruption via Hormuz), and s4_dev_debt (energy-import stress on frontier economies), but the primary home is s20.

china-ppi-surges-to-5-0-yoy-in-september.headline: China PPI surges to +5.0% YoY in September — fastest since June 2022 — driven by energy costs; domestic demand remains 'lackluster', creating stagflationary export dynamic
china-ppi-surges-to-5-0-yoy-in-september.summary: China's factory-gate prices rose 5.0% YoY in September (vs 4.4% forecast, 3.8% prior), the fastest pace since June 2022, driven by the Middle East energy shock rather than a domestic demand recovery. Analysts warn the pass-through from PPI inflation to CPI is limited due to weak household demand, creating a cost-push squeeze on Chinese manufacturers and a potential stagflationary export signal for global trade partners.

proposed_indicator.label: China PPI-CPI wedge (pp) — cost-push vs demand-pull signal
proposed_indicator.rubric: Difference between China PPI YoY and CPI YoY in percentage points. A large positive wedge (PPI >> CPI) indicates energy/commodity cost-push squeezing manufacturers without demand recovery — a stagflationary export signal. A large negative wedge (PPI << CPI) indicates deflationary factory-gate prices. Threshold: wedge >3pp = elevated concern; >5pp = high concern. Current (Sep 2026): PPI +5.0%, CPI roughly flat/slightly positive → wedge ~4–5pp.

china-ppi-surges-to-5-0-yoy-in-september.rationale: The existing s5 indicator tracks 'China PPI YoY (%) — large swing either way is worse,' which captures the directional risk. However, the current episode is qualitatively new: the PPI spike is energy-driven (external supply shock) while domestic demand stays weak, creating a PPI-CPI wedge that existing indicators don't differentiate. A +5pp PPI with near-flat CPI means Chinese exporters face margin compression and may ultimately export deflation to finished goods while importing inflation via energy — a dual-channel risk requiring its own indicator to track.

imf-gfsr-october-2026-identifies-ai-driv.headline: IMF GFSR October 2026 identifies AI-driven systemic cyber risk as a top-three catalyst for sharp financial-conditions tightening; hyperscalers now 10% of global IG bond issuance
imf-gfsr-october-2026-identifies-ai-driv.summary: The IMF's October 2026 Global Financial Stability Report names increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks — amplified by frontier AI — as one of three near-term catalysts (alongside AI asset correction and sovereign yield spikes) capable of triggering a sharp tightening of global financial conditions; separately, the report flags that hyperscalers now account for 10% of global investment-grade bond issuance (up from under 1% in 2024), concentrating both cyber and credit risk in the same set of entities.

proposed_story.name: AI-amplified cyber risk as systemic financial-stability threat
proposed_story.why: The IMF GFSR October 2026 elevates AI-enhanced cyberattacks to a top-three global financial-stability risk, co-equal with sovereign yield spikes and an AI-equity correction. Frontier AI models are increasing the sophistication of state-sponsored and criminal attacks on financial infrastructure. This is structurally new: the same AI buildout that is concentrating credit risk in hyperscalers (now 10% of IG issuance) is also generating the offensive cyber capability to attack the financial system's digital backbone — clearinghouses, payment rails, custodians. No existing story captures this intersection; s21_clearinghouses covers financial chokepoints operationally but not the cyber threat vector; s8_ai_capex covers the financing cycle but not the security externality.

indicators.label: Major financial-infrastructure cyber incident (0 none / 1 attempted/disrupted / 2 successful breach with systemic impact)
indicators.rubric: Track confirmed cyberattacks on systemically important financial institutions, payment systems, clearinghouses, or central banks. Score 0 if no material incidents; 1 if attack attempted or disrupted by defenses; 2 if successful breach causes operational outage, data exfiltration, or market disruption with systemic spillover. Source: CISA advisories, BIS, central bank disclosures, ISAC reports.

indicators.label: AI-offensive cyber capability escalation (0 stable / 1 elevated — state-actor use confirmed / 2 AI-generated attacks on financial infrastructure confirmed)
indicators.rubric: Track intelligence and vendor reports of AI-enhanced cyberattack tools targeting financial services. Score 0 if threat landscape stable; 1 if credible reports of state-sponsored or criminal groups deploying AI to enhance attack speed, evasion, or targeting of financial firms; 2 if AI-generated attacks are publicly attributed to a successful breach of a financial institution.

indicators.label: Hyperscaler IG bond concentration (% of global IG issuance)
indicators.rubric: Track the share of global investment-grade bond issuance by AI hyperscalers (Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, Apple, Oracle, CoreWeave). A rising share concentrates cyber and credit risk in the same entities. IMF benchmark: ~10% as of Oct 2026 (up from <1% in 2024). Threshold: >12% = elevated; >15% = high concentration risk.

imf-gfsr-october-2026-identifies-ai-driv.rationale: The IMF GFSR is the most authoritative global financial-stability publication and its explicit identification of AI-amplified cyber risk as a top-three systemic threat — alongside the RBA FSR's parallel finding about 'frontier AI models increasing the complexity of the international cyber threat landscape' — constitutes a material new risk not captured by any existing story. The novel structural feature is the feedback loop: AI capex concentrates IG bond issuance in hyperscalers while simultaneously generating offensive cyber tools that threaten the same financial system those bonds finance. This warrants a new story at proposed level 6 (real, rising, not yet acute) in Set 1 (financial plumbing).

bofa-estimates-ai-hyperscaler-capex-appr.headline: BofA estimates AI hyperscaler CapEx approaching $800bn in 2026 (+67% YoY), trending toward $1 trillion in 2027; capex-vs-revenue gap concern intensifying
bofa-estimates-ai-hyperscaler-capex-appr.summary: The IMF's October 13 World Economic Outlook (released at Bangkok Annual Meetings) explicitly flagged AI-investment borrowing by technology firms as compounding advanced-economy benchmark yield pressure, with public debt in advanced economies projected to reach 115% of GDP by 2031 from 108% in 2025; the GFSR (also released October 13) is expected to quantify AI capex debt risks in financial stability terms.
bofa-estimates-ai-hyperscaler-capex-appr.target_indicator: AI capex-vs-revenue gap concern (0 closing / 1 wide / 2 widening fast)
bofa-estimates-ai-hyperscaler-capex-appr.rationale: The IMF's explicit call-out of AI-investment borrowing as a source of advanced-economy yield pressure — at the flagship WEO level — is a material policy signal for s8_ai_capex. The AI capex-vs-revenue gap concern indicator should move toward '2 widening fast' given multilateral institutional recognition of the risk. This is not a new story but a significant escalation in the official narrative around an existing tracked risk.

china-s-nov-2026-extraterritorial-rare-e.headline: China's Nov-2026 extraterritorial rare-earth enforcement deadline is 4 months away; aerospace yttrium shortages already reported
china-s-nov-2026-extraterritorial-rare-e.summary: Following the Trump-Xi summit in Washington in late September 2026, China extended its one-year suspension of the expanded rare-earth export controls (originally due to expire November 10, 2026) until January 10, 2027, with no jointly documented critical-minerals settlement; the April 2025 controls on seven heavy REEs remain fully active, and the blacklist of 10 US and 14 EU firms imposed in June-July 2026 (including MP Materials and USA Rare Earth) was not lifted.
china-s-nov-2026-extraterritorial-rare-e.target_indicator: Nov-2025 pause status (0 extended / 1 expiring / 2 lapsed)
china-s-nov-2026-extraterritorial-rare-e.rationale: The pause status indicator for s6_rare_earths must be updated: the November 2026 expiry date has shifted to January 10, 2027, meaning the indicator moves from '1 expiring' back to '0 extended' — but only by 60 days and without a formal deal. Critically, the US domestic RE producer blacklist indicator should move to '1 entity-specific ban' given the June 2026 MOFCOM actions against MP Materials and USA Rare Earth. These are high-materiality changes to two existing indicators in the same story.

japan-10-year-jgb-yield-surges-to-2-7-2-.headline: Japan 10-Year JGB Yield Surges to ~2.7–2.8% (30-Year High), Yen Near 4-Decade Low; BOJ Hikes to 1%
japan-10-year-jgb-yield-surges-to-2-7-2-.summary: PM Takaichi's ¥10 trillion two-year consumption-tax cut is scheduled for submission to parliament in mid-October, but funding clarity remains elusive: the government pledged to avoid deficit-financing bonds yet has not identified an alternative revenue source. Oxford Economics has raised its end-2026 10Y JGB forecast to 2.8%; actual 10Y yields have already blown through that to 3.02% on Oct 12, with 30Y at 4.06%, pressuring carry-trade unwinds and JGB market functioning amid BoJ QT.
japan-10-year-jgb-yield-surges-to-2-7-2-.target_indicator: 30-year JGB yield (%) AND Takaichi plan financing clarity (0 ok / 1 unclear / 2 disorderly)
japan-10-year-jgb-yield-surges-to-2-7-2-.rationale: 30Y JGB is at 4.06% (data from Oct 12 Trading Economics), well above any prior tracker levels. The Takaichi financing-clarity indicator should move from 1 (unclear) toward 2 (disorderly): the mid-October bill submission without a credible funding mechanism was flagged explicitly by MUFG Research as 'a critical test.' Trump administration pressure on Japan's fiscal stance (noted by MUFG) adds an external layer. Both existing s2 indicators need immediate updates.

japan-us-coordinated-fx-intervention-jul.headline: Japan–US coordinated FX intervention July 31: structural yen weakness unresolved as BOJ faces fiscal-monetary trilemma
japan-us-coordinated-fx-intervention-jul.summary: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate 25bps to 1.25% in a split 7-2 decision on September 18, citing upside inflation risk, taking rates to their highest since 1995. The yen remains near 156-157 post-intervention (Japan and US conducted coordinated yen-buying in late July), while the 10-yr JGB yield sits at ~3.10% and the 30-yr at ~4.04%, with the curve reflecting both BOJ tightening trajectory and unresolved Takaichi fiscal risk premium.

proposed_indicator.label: US-Japan coordinated FX intervention flag (0 none / 1 unilateral BoJ / 2 joint US-Japan)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = no intervention; 1 = BoJ acting alone (standard); 2 = joint US Treasury + BoJ intervention signaling systemic yen stress. Current reading: 2. Reset to 1 when joint action ceases; to 0 after 90 days of market stability.

japan-us-coordinated-fx-intervention-jul.rationale: The US-Japan coordinated FX intervention in late July is a qualitative escalation not captured by the current USD/JPY level indicator alone. Coordinated intervention signals a geopolitical dimension to yen management (Treasury Secretary Bessent publicly confirmed US involvement), changing the risk topology: it creates a de facto floor but also a political tripwire if the yen depreciates past it again. This gap in the indicator set matters for carry-unwind risk assessment.
